title: Indian-Origin Woman Detained by ICE During Green Card Interview After Three Decades in US
excerpt: Babblejit 'Bubbly' Kaur, 60, was arrested during her biometrics appointment in Long Beach despite having an approved immigration petition and no criminal record.
body:
• Babblejit "Bubbly" Kaur, 60, was detained by ICE during what was supposed to be the final step of her green card process — a biometrics appointment at a Long Beach office.
  • Kaur has lived in the United States since 1994, ran a restaurant for over 20 years, and has no criminal record. Her husband holds a green card and two of her three children are US citizens.
  • She was transferred to Adelanto ICE detention facility, a former federal prison, where her family describes conditions as inhumane — lights kept on all night, limited visitation, and constant noise.
  • Congressman Robert Garcia has urged authorities to release her, calling the detention "horrific" and pledging to do everything possible to bring her home.

A 60-year-old Indian-origin woman who built her life in the United States over three decades was seized by federal agents during her green card biometrics appointment — the final step before receiving her permanent resident card. Babblejit "Bubbly" Kaur was arrested on December 1 at a US Immigration and Customs Enforcement office in Long Beach, California, according to her daughter Joti.

Arrested at the Front Desk

Kaur arrived at the ICE office for a scheduled appointment tied to her pending green card application. She already had an approved petition filed by her elder daughter, a US citizen, and supported by her husband, a lawful permanent resident, according to a Long Beach Watchdog report.

While Kaur was at the front desk, several federal agents entered the building. She was called into a separate room and told she was being arrested, Joti told local media. Though Kaur was permitted an eight-minute phone call with her attorney, she was not released.

"She was really scared. She was loaded into a van full of men with her hands and feet shackled."

— Joti, Bubbly Kaur's daughter

For several hours, the family had no information about where she had been taken. They later discovered she had been moved overnight to Adelanto, a former federal prison in San Bernardino County now operating as an ICE detention facility.

Three Decades of Community Roots

Kaur immigrated to the United States in 1994 and initially lived in Laguna Beach before settling in Long Beach's Belmont Shore neighborhood. She and her husband are parents to three children — Joti, 34, who has legal status under the Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals program, and an older son and daughter who are both US citizens.

For more than 20 years, the couple ran Natraj Cuisine of India and Nepal, a restaurant on 2nd Street in Belmont Shore that became a fixture in the local community, the Long Beach Watchdog reported. Kaur also worked for nearly 25 years at a Belmont Shore Rite Aid until the chain shuttered its remaining stores earlier in 2025. She had recently been preparing to return to the restaurant industry at Royal Indian Curry House.

Her family and public records confirm she has no criminal history.

Conditions at Adelanto

Family members described harsh conditions at the Adelanto facility. Kaur is being held in a large dormitory-style room with dozens of other detainees. Lights reportedly stay on throughout the night, and constant noise makes sleep difficult, the family told IndiaWest.

Visitation is restricted. Family members must often wait an entire day for a brief meeting with Kaur.

"This has been a nightmare. We are trying every possible option to bring her home. She should not be there. The conditions are extremely inhumane."

— Joti, speaking to IndiaWest

Political Response and Growing Pressure

Democratic Congressman Robert Garcia, who represents the Long Beach area, publicly condemned the detention. "We have been in touch with the family of Bubbly. We are going to do everything we can to bring her home," Garcia said in a statement. "These horrific actions continue to terrorize hardworking and good people who are trying to make our community a better place."

Garcia's office said he has been communicating with federal agencies about the case while Kaur's family pursues additional legal filings that could make her eligible for release on bond.

A Broader Pattern

Kaur's case is not isolated. Immigration attorneys have reported a growing trend of US Customs and Border Protection officers targeting elderly Indian green card holders, particularly those who spend extended periods visiting family in India. In several cases, officers have pressured elderly Indians to voluntarily surrender their green cards by signing Form I-407, according to Florida-based immigration attorney Ashwin Sharma.

Approximately 2,400 Indian nationals have been deported from the US since President Donald Trump intensified removal operations. The Department of Homeland Security has not offered an official explanation for Kaur's arrest despite her lawful presence and approved immigration petition.

For Indian Americans and NRIs following immigration proceedings, Kaur's case underscores the importance of having legal representation at every interaction with immigration authorities — even appointments that appear routine.
nri_angle: An Indian-origin woman who built her life in the US for 30 years was detained during her green card biometrics appointment, highlighting growing ICE enforcement risks for the diaspora.
author: Diaspora Desk
